rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while ensuring strongly retained compounds elute. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty and measure how the critical pairs respond to slope. The initial run has substantial resolution margin, so a faster gradient may preserve full separation.

Test whether higher temperature separates the critical cluster through selectivity changes while retaining the fast gradient. This also establishes the temperature response without changing the solvent program.

Use an intermediate temperature to avoid the high-temperature co-elution, with a slightly shallower gradient to improve separation in the central cluster. This targets full resolution with only a modest increase in retention time.

Raise temperature by one grid step to open the remaining critical pair. The neighboring pair still has resolution margin at 50 C, so 55 C may balance both separations while keeping the time penalty at zero.

Injection 5 already reaches the maximum possible CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a slightly higher starting organic fraction to seek a shorter, equally scoring method while checking its effect on the two marginally resolved pairs.

Injection 5 remains optimal at CRF 1.000. Test a faster gradient at 50 C to seek another maximum-scoring method, using slope-induced selectivity changes to separate the central cluster without approaching the high-temperature co-elution.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness around the maximum-scoring method to test whether the two critical pairs gain a better resolution balance. The last peak should remain well within the gradient, with only a small increase in retention time.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test lower-temperature selectivity as an alternative route to full resolution with a shorter gradient. Cooling may separate the critical cluster in the opposite elution order while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty window.

Combine the higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to recover the separation lost in injection 6. This may preserve CRF 1.000 while balancing the two critical pairs more evenly than injection 8.

One further reduction in gradient steepness should lift the R 1.47 pair above 1.5 while preserving the other critical separation. The last peak is expected near 8 minutes, targeting another maximum-scoring method with a more balanced resolution margin.

With the maximum CRF secured, test a faster, high-temperature alternative that may move the previously co-eluting pair past its selectivity crossover. Raising the starting organic fraction should further shift that pair, though early-peak retention must be checked.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step to try to open the remaining critical pair on the high-temperature branch. Check whether the first two peaks and the adjacent central pair retain sufficient separation; injection 5 remains the maximum-scoring benchmark.

Return to the successful 55 C region with a slope between injections 10 and 11, targeting balanced resolution above 1.5 for both critical pairs. The lower endpoint remains above the observed elution window, so all compounds should elute during the gradient.

Test whether a higher starting fraction combined with a shallower slope preserves full resolution and improves the critical-pair balance. Early peaks should remain retained at 55 C, and the last peak should still elute near the zero-time-penalty window.

Trim the maximum-scoring method’s unused high-organic tail while preserving its gradient slope exactly. The last peak previously eluted near 0.57 organic fraction, so a 0.65 endpoint should keep all peaks within the gradient and retain CRF 1.000.

Test a steeper gradient on the high-temperature selectivity branch to open the pair that remained unresolved in injection 12, while lowering the starting fraction to protect early-peak separation. This explores a faster alternative; the established CRF 1.000 methods remain optimal benchmarks.

Test a slightly steeper slope than the maximum-scoring method to locate the faster edge of its full-resolution window. This should shorten retention modestly, although the R 1.59 pair may become limiting.

Trim injection 11’s gradient to just above the last peak’s estimated elution fraction while preserving its slope and improved minimum resolution. This targets CRF 1.000 with a shorter programmed gradient; the last peak should still elute before the gradient ends at the outlet.

Test one temperature step below injection 7 to see whether the fast-gradient central cluster separates better after its elution-order crossover. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this probes a shorter alternative without replacing the established best method.

Preserve the successful gradient slope through the nine earlier peaks, then test a lower-organic hold for the isolated final compound. This explores a shorter programmed gradient while checking whether the final peak still elutes within the zero-time-penalty window.

Slightly flatten injection 11’s gradient to test additional resolution margin while using the zero-time-penalty window demonstrated by injection 21. The last peak should elute around 8.4 minutes, with both critical pairs expected to remain above R 1.5.

Flatten injection 15’s gradient to recover its limiting separation while retaining the larger margin for the other critical pair. This tests whether a higher-starting-organic method can also achieve CRF 1.000; the established maximum-scoring methods remain the benchmarks.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 23 to lift its R 1.41 pair above 1.5 while preserving the other critical separation. The last peak is expected near 9 minutes, testing whether improved resolution still fits within the zero-time-penalty window.

Use a slope between the maximum-scoring injections 11 and 22, targeting full resolution with the last peak near 8.2 minutes. The campaign has already reached the absolute maximum CRF of 1.000; this final run checks another nearby method without repeating a tested setting.
